reviews.comment: I didn't have a super hard time with this class because I already knew how to code in Python. However, this class was a hard time for students who didn't know how to code in Python already - professor barely taught, just reading off the slides. Exams were also pretty weird- with some stuff we had never learned before on the exams.

Dr. Moore is one of the most kind and welcoming professors at TAMU. I missed the 1st two weeks of school due to having surgery, but she was very lenient with my absences. She was easily accessible for office hours and by following her advice, I was able to get an A in the class despite having no coding experience. I wish she was teaching ENGR216!

Dr. Moore is so sweet, she gave us duckies at the beginning of the school year and she's so fun. Engineering 102 is a pretty standard class, but she teaches it really well and makes you have fun with it! If you get the chance, take her class :)

Dr. Moore was an effective professor for Engr 102, and made the class feel welcoming. TA's and Zybooks provide all the assistance you really need for this class, so I don't understand the negative reviews. I did not have a lot of coding experience and was still able to succeed in this class. Dr. Moore is very reasonable and made 102 a great class!

We had a lecture where we were doing practice problems but the questions were missing info bc she used ChatGPT to make them. Super disorganized overall, canvas due dates weren't correct like 80% of the time bc they were imported from last year. She took attendance for extra credit.

Dr. Moore was a nice lady but not a good prof! She does not prepare you for any of the homeworks and leaves you struggling unless you already have a lot of coding experiences. Also only gives 1 week to work on each homework while some of the other profs give 2 weeks or more.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is funny. However, doesn't teach well if you are completely new to coding/Python, as she just reads over the  slides and it seems like she doesn't know what she's talking about half the time. Eye out the smartest kids in the room somehow on the first day or get lucky and you'll be fine. Ask questions in the discord to get help from PTs.

Most of the work done in the class is auto-graded, so a good bit of time is spent trying to output exactly how the computer wants it. The professor is very nice and the quizzes based on the lectures are not too difficult. The midterm is quite manageable, but the final was more difficult. If you put in the effort, an A is not too hard.

Awesome personality. Kind/understanding prof. Willing to help students if they show effort in at least attempting to learn the material. TA's help teach the class and lectures are just powerpoint presentations.

Notice the positive reviews do not speak to her teaching ability and only her personality. She's a bio & ag professor and she SHOULD NOT be teaching a python class. She has no idea what she is talking about and blindly reads off of lecture slides and cannot help you at all. Her TA's do everything, and although she's funny at times, DON'T TAKE HER.

Dr. Moore is a hilarious and personable teacher that makes going to class fun. Though the material given by the university to teach can deviate into monotony, her approach to engaging lectures and building genuine relationships with her students makes her an outstanding person to learn from.

The whole class was pretty much a review for me so I can't say much about her teaching but I think her teaching and lectures are decent. However, she was a really nice teacher. She was laid-back in class and liked to make jokes all class. She was also lenient with turning stuff in late.
I had prior coding experience, so I wont speak to Dr. Moore's teaching ability. I really appreciated her laid-back personality and honesty with the class. Overall, not a bad experience.

Dr. Moore has a great personality, and she graded very nicely. However, she is not a great teacher, and at times it seems like she doesn't even understand how to execute the code. The peer tutors for the class were also no help, so unless you have prior coding experience, get ready to rely on the textbook and stack exchange.
